subject: Saddlepoint gateway pattern for private VPC — topology & ops playbook
messages:
From: Alex Grant <eng@sunnyhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC: question about tenant edge/gateway pattern

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our netops team kicked off a quick review of the private deployment options for SunnyHealth's on‑prem sites. One open question: we need a pattern that lets us keep a very tight data egress policy while still giving Redwood's control plane the necessary connectivity for telemetry, agent registration, and model updates.

Current constraints:
- Strict egress: only a single outbound TLS destination allowed (we need to minimize approved FQDNs/IPs).
- No inbound holes allowed to tenant network.
- MTU variations across our colos (9000 in colo A, 1500 in colo B).
- We prefer not to run BGP inside tenant racks.

Do you have a recommendation on a gateway pattern that centralizes the demarc point and still preserves control/data separation? We called it an "edge gateway" in our notes — would appreciate any reference diagrams or runbook items you can share.

Thanks — happy to schedule a short sync if easier.

—Alex
Alex Grant
Cloud Infrastructure Lead, SunnyHealth
eng@sunnyhealth.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <eng@sunnyhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, netops@acme-cloud.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: question about tenant edge/gateway pattern

Alex — thanks for the clear constraints, that's exactly the kind of input we need. Short answer: we recommend the pattern we've been prototyping internally which we're calling the "saddlepoint gateway."

High level (two bullets):
- Saddlepoint gateway = a hardened tenant demarc (single outbound egress endpoint) that terminates all tenant traffic destined for Redwood services. It preserves separation by running the control plane connector in a dedicated namespace/process with strict localhost sockets/KV cache separation from the data path.
- Connectivity uses outbound TLS tunnels (mutual TLS) from the gateway to a regional Redwood ingress pool. No inbound ports into tenant network are required. We avoid BGP inside the tenant by using static routes or a small set of cloud NAT translations for service IPs.

Key notes for your constraints:
- Single outbound FQDN: the gateway will proxy/route all egress through one FQDN (we provide a small set of IPs per region).
- No inbound holes: all control messages from Redwood are delivered over established outbound tunnels; agent registration is initiated from tenant side.
- MTU: we recommend MTU discovery and an MTU‑aware forwarder on the saddlepoint. We include a config snippet in the attached ops playbook for MSS clamping and jumbo frame fallbacks.
- BGP: not required. Use static VRF routes on the gateway or a simple next‑hop learned from the colo router.

Operational/HA pattern (summary):
1) Two redundant saddlepoint gateways in the tenant demarc (active/standby).
2) Health probe + local L3 failover (keepalived) with session preservation via sticky KV cache sync over the control tunnel.
3) Local caching for model artifacts and prefix caching for hot prefixes to avoid egress spikes.
4) Observability: a per‑gateway telemetry stream (metrics + tokenized traces) forwarded over the control tunnel; we do not put raw logs on the same channel unless agreed.

I've attached a short pattern brief (saddlepoint‑pattern‑v1.pdf) and a draft ops playbook (ops‑playbook‑draft.md) with runbook steps for cutover, failover, and MTU testing. Jonas — I flagged a few routing/HA questions inline in the playbook where we'd like your input. Kimberly — please check the compliance bits for egress proofing.

If useful, we can do a 30‑minute architecture review this week and walk the diagrams. Proposed times: Thu 10–11am PT or Fri 2–3pm PT.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
Redwood Inference — Private Deployments

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private VPC: question about tenant edge/gateway pattern

Thanks Soojin — nice writeup. Quick inline notes and suggested ops checklist additions:

> Saddlepoint gateway = a hardened tenant demarc (single outbound egress endpoint) that terminates all tenant traffic destined for Redwood services.
- Confirm: saddlepoint handles both control plane (tunnels, telemetry) and data egress, but runs them as isolated processes with separate TLS identities. We need a clear boundary: control TLS certs minted by customer KMS; data path certs minted by Redwood or customer depending on compliance.

Routing and HA:
- Prefer static default route from tenant racks to the saddlepoint (simple and predictable).
- Keepalived with VRRP for VIP failover; use connection tracking sync for session handoff (we provide the sync hook in the playbook).
- For jumbo frame islands: configure per‑port MTU on the saddlepoint and enable MSS clamping on outbound NAT to avoid fragmentation to Redwood endpoints. Add an automated MTU test during cutover (we put the runner in the playbook).

Security/compliance ops items:
- Egress allowlist: list the minimal IP ranges per region (Ops will supply per‑region CIDR).
- Evidence: include a runbook step to capture tcpdump summary + signed manifest for auditors.

Cutover checklist (additions):
- Preflight: validate DNS resolution to saddlepoint FQDN, validate TLS pinning for control identity.
- Staging sync: prepopulate model cache using controlled fetch window to avoid cold‑start thundering.
- Traffic shaping: enable rate caps for early hours (first 48 hrs) and monitor token rate.

I've attached a revised diagram with the VIP pair and control tunnel breakout labeled (saddlepoint‑diagram‑v2.png). I can be on the call Thu 10:30am PT to walk it if that works.

Jonas
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
